original_value: AbstractComputational models can help researchers to interpret data, understand biological functions, and make quantitative predictions. The Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML) is a file format for representing computational models in a declarative form that different software systems can exchange. SBML is oriented towards describing biological processes of the sort common in research on a number of topics, including metabolic pathways, cell signaling pathways, and many others. By supporting SBML as an input/output format, different tools can all operate on an identical representation of a model, removing opportunities for translation errors and assuring a common starting point for analyses and simulations. This document provides the specification for Release 2 of Version 2 of SBML Level 3 Core. The specification defines the data structures prescribed by SBML as well as their encoding in XML, the eXtensible Markup Language. Release 2 corrects some errors and clarifies some ambiguities discovered in Release 1. This specification also defines validation rules that determine the validity of an SBML document, and provides many examples of models in SBML form. Other materials and software are available from the SBML project website at http://sbml.org/.

result.paraphrase: Abstract computational models aid researchers in interpreting data, understanding biological functions, and making quantitative predictions. The Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML) is a file format for expressing computational models declaratively so that different software systems can exchange them. SBML is intended for describing biological processes commonly studied in areas such as metabolic pathways, cell signaling pathways, and many others. When tools support SBML as both input and output, they can all work from the same model representation, eliminating translation errors and providing a shared baseline for analyses and simulations. This document specifies Release 2 of Version 2 of SBML Level 3 Core. It defines the SBML-prescribed data structures and their XML (eXtensible Markup Language) encoding. Release 2 fixes some errors and clarifies ambiguities found in Release 1. The specification also sets out validation rules for determining whether an SBML document is valid, and includes many example models in SBML form. Additional materials and software are available from the SBML project website at http://sbml.org/.
